title: The Most Lucrative AI Business to Start in 2027
titleZh: 2027 年最值得创办的 AI 业务
subtitle: A Full Guide to Becoming a One-Person Creative Team
subtitleZh: 成为单人创意团队的完整指南
author: Dan Koe
description: Dan Koe explores the most lucrative AI-powered business opportunity for individuals in 2027: becoming a one-person creative team. The article explains how to capture attention, build an irreplaceable personal brand, use AI for content research and strategy, and acquire the first client.
descriptionZh: Dan Koe 探讨了 2027 年个人最值得尝试的 AI 创业方向：成为一支单人创意团队。文章从注意力获取出发，讲解如何打造不可替代的个人品牌、借助 AI 进行内容研究与策略规划，以及如何获得第一位客户。

chapters.title: You Will Either Become a Creator, Pay a Creator, or Get Paid to Work for a Creator
chapters.titleZh: 你终将成为创作者、付费雇佣创作者，或为创作者工作

paragraphs.en: The most lucrative skill has always been capturing attention.
paragraphs.zh: 最赚钱的技能，一直都是获取注意力。

paragraphs.en: It’s obvious why.
paragraphs.zh: 原因显而易见。

paragraphs.en: If your goal is making more money, it doesn’t matter how good a software you build. It doesn’t matter if it took you 3 years and endless scrapped drafts to write a book. It doesn’t matter if you work hard and improve yourself to increase your career opportunities.
paragraphs.zh: 如果你的目标是赚更多的钱，那么你开发的软件有多优秀，并不重要。你花了三年时间、经历无数次草稿推翻与重写，最终完成了一本书，也不重要。即使你努力工作、不断提升自己，希望借此获得更多职业机会，这些本身也不足以保证成功。

paragraphs.en: If nobody knows who you are or what you offer, how in the world are they going to pay you?
paragraphs.zh: 如果没有人知道你是谁，也不知道你能提供什么，他们又怎么可能愿意为你付钱呢？

paragraphs.en: Meaning, whatever your work is or whatever business you build, capturing attention and acquiring customers will be the primary thing that determines your success.
paragraphs.zh: 换句话说，无论你从事什么工作，或正在建立什么样的事业，获取注意力和赢得客户，才是决定你能否成功的核心因素。

paragraphs.en: This applies to both your own business and others’ businesses.
paragraphs.zh: 这既适用于你自己的事业，也适用于别人的生意。

paragraphs.en: And other people will pay top dollar for you to do it for them.
paragraphs.zh: 而且，别人愿意为你替他们完成这件事支付高额报酬。

paragraphs.en: As job security goes down, people are met with 3 options:
paragraphs.zh: 随着工作的稳定性不断下降，人们将面临三个选择：

paragraphs.en: 1. Complain about how life is unfair and do nothing.
paragraphs.zh: 1. 抱怨生活不公平，然后什么也不做。

paragraphs.en: 2. Upskill and reeducate to find a better job opportunity.
paragraphs.zh: 2. 学习新技能、重新接受教育，寻找更好的工作机会。

paragraphs.en: 3. Start building the business you’ve always wanted to build.
paragraphs.zh: 3. 开始建立自己一直想要创办的事业。

paragraphs.en: An absurd amount of people will choose option 3.
paragraphs.zh: 将会有数量惊人的人选择第三条路。

paragraphs.en: As you could guess, and as everyone is screaming about on social media, the way they will build that business is by starting a personal brand.
paragraphs.zh: 正如你所猜到的，也正如社交媒体上所有人都在反复强调的那样，他们建立事业的方式，就是打造个人品牌。

paragraphs.en: Why?
paragraphs.zh: 为什么？

paragraphs.en: Because attention is a finite resource, and it’s only becoming more scarce. People can make more money, but they will never get back the attention they spent.
paragraphs.zh: 因为注意力是一种有限资源，而且只会变得越来越稀缺。人们可以赚到更多的钱，却永远无法找回已经消耗掉的注意力。

paragraphs.en: In this letter, I will show you how to master attention capture on social media. That way, at least for the next few years, you won’t have an issue making money.
paragraphs.zh: 在这篇文章中，我将向你展示如何掌握在社交媒体上获取注意力的方法。这样，至少在未来几年里，你就不必再为赚钱而发愁。

paragraphs.en: With what you learn, you can start your own business using social media to fuel it, or become a “one person creative team” for other companies that will pay top dollar for your skill set.
paragraphs.zh: 通过这里学到的东西，你既可以利用社交媒体为自己的事业引流，也可以成为其他公司的「单人创意团队」，凭借自己的技能获得丰厚报酬。

paragraphs.en: Promo - Workshops for the Second Renaissance: I’m teaming up with Hussain Ibarra (grew from 2,600 to 20,100 Substack subs) to teach newsletter and article writing that people actually want to read.
paragraphs.zh: 推广——第二次文艺复兴系列工作坊：我将与 Hussain Ibarra 合作。他的 Substack 订阅人数从 2,600 人增长到了 20,100 人。我们将一起教授如何写出真正让人愿意阅读的新闻通讯和文章。

paragraphs.en: If you’ve considered building a Substack, or want to write better X articles, sign up here, it’s $49 but will teach you the skills to make far more than that.
paragraphs.zh: 如果你考虑过建立自己的 Substack，或者希望写出更好的 X 长文，可以报名参加。课程费用为 49 美元，但它将教会你掌握能够创造远超这一金额价值的技能。

paragraphs.en: The data is almost too hard to ignore.
paragraphs.zh: 相关数据已经明显到几乎无法忽视。

paragraphs.en: Goldman Sachs predicts the creator economy will nearly double, from $250 billion in 2023 to $480 billion by 2027.
paragraphs.zh: 高盛预测，创作者经济的规模将接近翻倍，从 2023 年的 2,500 亿美元增长到 2027 年的 4,800 亿美元。

paragraphs.en: In 2025, creators earned about $185 billion in ad revenue, which is the first year they passed traditional media.
paragraphs.zh: 2025 年，创作者获得的广告收入约为 1,850 亿美元。这也是创作者的广告收入首次超过传统媒体的一年。

paragraphs.en: US brands spent $13.9 billion on creators in 2021, and the IAB expects that to reach $43.9 billion in 2026, which is about 3x in 5 years.
paragraphs.zh: 2021 年，美国品牌在创作者身上投入了 139 亿美元。互动广告局（IAB）预计，到 2026 年这一数字将达到 439 亿美元，也就是五年内增长到原来的三倍左右。

paragraphs.en: Absurd.
paragraphs.zh: 这实在惊人。

paragraphs.en: And as someone who both is a creator, has worked for creators, and pays creators, the prices people charge are crazy. There is an absurd amount of VC money being thrown around, paying thousands of dollars for a single reel or 60-second YouTube time slot (that don’t even bring results 90% of the time).
paragraphs.zh: 作为一个既是创作者、曾为创作者工作，又会付费聘请创作者的人，我发现这个行业的收费已经高得惊人。大量风险投资资金正在涌入这个领域，企业愿意为一条 Reels 短视频，或者 YouTube 视频中仅仅 60 秒的广告时段支付数千美元——而这些推广有 90% 的时候甚至无法带来实际效果。

paragraphs.en: The point is that social media is where the attention is. Not the radio, TV, or news anymore. When you want to start any kind of business - from lifestyle business talking about your interests to the next unicorn startup, posting content is almost a given at this point for how you attract an audience that pays you.
paragraphs.zh: 关键在于，注意力如今集中在社交媒体上，而不再是广播、电视或传统新闻媒体。如果你想创办任何一种事业，无论是围绕个人兴趣建立生活方式型企业，还是打造下一家独角兽创业公司，发布内容几乎已经成为吸引愿意为你付费的受众的必经之路。

paragraphs.en: When companies want to expand, they put millions of dollars into affiliate and partnership campaigns. I keep getting ads from Hormozi saying they pay over a million a month to creators to promote Skool. And that’s aside the fact the Hormozi is a creator, which massively helps grow Skool.
paragraphs.zh: 当公司想要扩大业务时，它们会投入数百万美元开展联盟营销和合作推广活动。我不断看到 Hormozi 的广告，他表示自己每个月要支付超过一百万美元给创作者，让他们推广 Skool。更不用说 Hormozi 本人就是一名创作者，这一身份本身也极大地推动了 Skool 的增长。

paragraphs.en: “Founder-led marketing” is now a buzzword in the startup space, which essentially means that the latest and greatest way to grow your startup is... you guessed it, starting a personal brand and posting content (and most of them are horrible at it by the way, and you should probably start using Eden to research, differentiate yourself, and post).
paragraphs.zh: 「创始人主导营销」（Founder-led marketing）如今已经成为创业圈的流行词。它本质上意味着，发展初创企业最新、最有效的方式就是……你猜对了：打造个人品牌并持续发布内容。顺便说一句，大多数创始人在这方面做得相当糟糕，所以你或许应该开始使用 Eden 来进行研究、建立差异化，并发布内容。

paragraphs.en: What does this mean for you?
paragraphs.zh: 那么，这对你意味着什么？

paragraphs.en: It doesn’t matter if you plan to work for yourself, have a business already, or want to work for another business - the most lucrative skill to learn is capturing attention. When you translate that to the digital landscape, the most lucrative skill is creating content - good content, not infinite slop.
paragraphs.zh: 无论你打算为自己工作、已经拥有一家企业，还是希望进入其他公司工作，最值得学习的技能都是获取注意力。当这一技能被放到数字世界中时，它就意味着创造内容——真正优秀的内容，而不是无穷无尽的垃圾内容。

paragraphs.en: Unfortunately, you can master capturing attention, but that doesn’t mean you’ve actually captured it.
paragraphs.zh: 遗憾的是，你即使掌握了获取注意力的方法，也不意味着你真的已经获得了注意力。

paragraphs.en: Getting a million views on one tweet or reel is useless if the rest of your posts get a thousand views a pop. That signals that your content is decent, but your brand is non-existent. We need both.
paragraphs.zh: 如果你的一条推文或 Reels 短视频获得了一百万次浏览，而其他内容每条只有一千次浏览，那么这次爆红其实毫无意义。这说明你的内容还不错，但你的品牌根本不存在。我们需要同时拥有这两样东西。

paragraphs.en: You can try to go viral all the time, which is what most people do (and why most people fail abysmally), or you can build a world of content that people can’t help but explore.
paragraphs.zh: 你可以像大多数人一样，不断尝试制造爆款——这也是大多数人惨败的原因；或者，你可以建立一个内容世界，让人们忍不住想要不断探索。

paragraphs.en: I’ll teach you how to do that.
paragraphs.zh: 接下来，我会教你如何做到这一点。

paragraphs.en: There is a massive shift happening in the content space right now.
paragraphs.zh: 当下，内容行业正在发生一场巨大的转变。

paragraphs.en: I’m the founder of Eden, a tool where creators and digital businesses research viral ideas, plan and schedule their content, sell digital products, and run their email list.
paragraphs.zh: 我是 Eden 的创始人。这是一款工具，创作者和数字企业可以利用它研究热门创意、规划和安排内容发布、销售数字产品，以及管理自己的邮件订阅列表。

paragraphs.en: That’s not meant to be a pitch. It’s to point out that we have data about this that almost nobody else has. We know what topics, hooks, and content styles work across billions of posts.
paragraphs.zh: 我提到这些并不是为了推销产品，而是想说明，我们掌握着几乎没有其他人拥有的数据。通过数十亿条帖子，我们知道哪些主题、开头钩子和内容风格真正有效。

paragraphs.en: Aside that, freelancers and agencies use it to run their clients’ personal brand, from content to email marketing to digital product launches and building funnels.
paragraphs.zh: 除此之外，自由职业者和代理机构也会使用它来运营客户的个人品牌，工作范围涵盖内容创作、邮件营销、数字产品发布以及营销漏斗搭建。

paragraphs.en: We talk with these content agencies and media teams, and they are all saying the same things (paraphrasing):
paragraphs.zh: 我们与这些内容代理机构和媒体团队交流时，听到的基本都是同样的观点。以下是经过转述的内容：

paragraphs.en: “We’re not firing people yet, but we can take on so much more work without expanding the team because everyone’s output has gone up.”
paragraphs.zh: 「我们目前还没有裁员，但由于每个人的产出都提高了，即使不扩大团队规模，我们也能承接更多工作。」

paragraphs.en: “The reason creators and founders hire us is because they don’t even have time to think about content. They have a team to manage and a business to run, which requires focus. AI can write content for them, but they still know they need a strategist or creative director who leverages AI better than they would. It still requires creativity and thought.”
paragraphs.zh: 「创作者和创始人聘请我们的原因，是他们甚至没有时间思考内容。他们需要管理团队、经营企业，这些事情都需要集中精力。AI 可以替他们写内容，但他们仍然知道，自己需要一位策略师或创意总监，能够比他们更好地运用 AI。这项工作依然需要创造力和思考。」

paragraphs.en: “AI still can’t write the best posts, and I don’t think it ever will, but it can research what’s performing, understand the strategy, and draft posts that are almost there. My entire job nowadays is reviewing and rewriting drafts. It takes me 4 hours a day instead of 12 now.”
paragraphs.zh: 「AI 目前仍然写不出最优秀的帖子，我认为它可能永远也做不到这一点。但它能够研究哪些内容表现出色、理解背后的策略，并生成已经相当接近成品的初稿。如今，我的全部工作就是审核并重写这些草稿。过去每天需要 12 个小时，现在只需要 4 个小时。」

paragraphs.en: The most lucrative AI business to start (as one person), in my eyes, is two-fold.
paragraphs.zh: 在我看来，一个人最值得创办的 AI 业务有两个方向。

paragraphs.en: One - you can become your own creative team. Start a personal brand. Build an audience. Create digital products. Build an email list. All that stuff. And that is your sole focus. Trust me when I say it is a full-time job, even with AI. If you are a creator, you probably aren’t going to build software without a team.
paragraphs.zh: 第一，你可以成为自己的创意团队。打造个人品牌，积累受众，开发数字产品，建立邮件订阅列表，完成所有这些事情，并将其作为自己的全部工作重点。相信我，即使有了 AI，这依然是一份全职工作。如果你是一名创作者，很可能无法在没有团队的情况下同时开发软件。

paragraphs.en: Two - you can become someone else’s creative team. Help companies, founders, and even creators who don’t have the creative bandwidth to put out irreplaceable content. Most founders still create “announcement” style content and have no idea what it takes to build influence online.
paragraphs.zh: 第二，你可以成为别人的创意团队。帮助那些缺乏创作精力、无法持续产出不可替代内容的公司、创始人，甚至其他创作者。大多数创始人仍然只会发布「公告式」内容，完全不了解如何在网上建立影响力。

paragraphs.en: In other words, you become the creative director of your own brand or someone else’s.
paragraphs.zh: 换句话说，你将成为自己品牌或他人品牌的创意总监。

paragraphs.en: If you can pull this off, I don’t see why you wouldn’t be able to demand a price that is a fraction of what a full team costs. $10-$75k a month for 1-3 clients isn’t that far out of reach (if you’re good at this and practice - don’t let your mind convince you this is your next opportunity to get rich quick). And business owners who pour millions into marketing won’t bat an eye at that price.
paragraphs.zh: 如果你能够做好这件事，我不明白你为什么不能收取相当于完整团队成本一小部分的费用。服务 1 至 3 位客户，每月收取 1 万至 7.5 万美元，并非完全遥不可及——前提是你确实擅长这项工作，并且不断练习。不要让自己误以为这又是一个快速致富的机会。那些每年投入数百万美元进行营销的企业主，面对这样的价格甚至可能不会皱一下眉头。

paragraphs.en: What does this one person creative team look like?
paragraphs.zh: 那么，这支单人创意团队究竟是什么样的？

paragraphs.en: What skills do you need to learn?
paragraphs.zh: 你又需要学习哪些技能？

paragraphs.en: Job 1) Brand Strategist
paragraphs.zh: 职位一：品牌策略师

paragraphs.en: A brand strategist is in charge of positioning and perception.
paragraphs.zh: 品牌策略师负责品牌定位以及外界对品牌的认知。

paragraphs.en: They are going to be the first to say that you shouldn’t just follow trends and try to go viral with every post. Growth and engagement are important, but not at the expense of trust and authority.
paragraphs.zh: 他们首先会告诉你，不应该只是追逐潮流，试图让每一篇帖子都成为爆款。增长和互动固然重要，但不能以牺牲信任与权威性为代价。

paragraphs.en: I’m going to show you how to do all of this below, by the way.
paragraphs.zh: 顺便说一句，下面我就会向你展示如何完成这些工作。

paragraphs.en: 2) Content Strategist
paragraphs.zh: 职位二：内容策略师

paragraphs.en: Not the same as a brand strategist.
paragraphs.zh: 这与品牌策略师并不是同一个角色。

paragraphs.en: The content strategist is someone who scouts what content is performing in various topics and niches and proposes what the creator’s next posts should be. They deeply study post formats, YouTube thumbnail and title structures, retention, and virality.
paragraphs.zh: 内容策略师负责研究不同主题和细分领域中表现出色的内容，并据此提出创作者下一步应该发布什么。他们会深入研究帖子形式、YouTube 缩略图与标题结构、观看留存率，以及内容传播的爆发力。

paragraphs.en: They are good at growing accounts, but without accounting for brand strategy, if the creator were to stop posting, nobody would ask where they went.
paragraphs.zh: 他们擅长让账号增长，但如果没有品牌策略作为支撑，一旦创作者停止发布内容，就不会有人关心他们去了哪里。

paragraphs.en: 3) Content Writer / Social Media Manager
paragraphs.zh: 职位三：内容撰稿人／社交媒体经理

paragraphs.en: The person who drafts the tweets, YouTube or Reels scripts, X articles, and Substack newsletters, plans them, and posts them.
paragraphs.zh: 这个角色负责撰写推文、YouTube 或 Reels 视频脚本、X 长文以及 Substack 新闻通讯，同时负责规划内容并发布。

paragraphs.en: They take the content strategists ideas and brand strategists direction and make sure the content aligns with that.
paragraphs.zh: 他们根据内容策略师提出的创意和品牌策略师制定的方向，确保最终发布的内容与整体策略保持一致。

paragraphs.en: You can probably tell why most people are failing to build anything lasting with AI. They still treat it as a get rich quick scheme. They think that if they just have Claude pump out scripts without direction or data they’re going to magically build a connection with their audience.
paragraphs.zh: 你大概已经明白，为什么大多数人无法利用 AI 建立真正持久的事业了。他们依然把 AI 当作快速致富的工具，以为只要让 Claude 不断生成脚本，即使没有明确方向，也没有数据支持，就能神奇地与受众建立联系。

paragraphs.en: Almost nobody accounts for brand strategy.
paragraphs.zh: 几乎没有人真正考虑品牌策略。

paragraphs.en: Some people account for content strategy.
paragraphs.zh: 有些人会考虑内容策略。

paragraphs.en: Most people just turn random ideas into posts and pray that they’ll do well.
paragraphs.zh: 而大多数人只是把随机想到的点子变成帖子，然后祈祷它们能够获得不错的表现。

paragraphs.en: This is your competition, and it’s not hard to stand out.
paragraphs.zh: 这就是你所面对的竞争者，而想要脱颖而出，其实并不困难。

chapters.title: If You Were My Client, Here’s Exactly How I’d Build an Irreplaceable Personal Brand
chapters.titleZh: 如果你是我的客户，我会这样一步步打造一个不可替代的个人品牌

paragraphs.en: Let’s have some fun with this.
paragraphs.zh: 让我们来做点有意思的事情。

paragraphs.en: I’m going to act like I’m onboarding you as a client.
paragraphs.zh: 接下来，我会假设自己正在为你办理客户入驻。

paragraphs.en: That way, if you want to become a creator, you can implement the process yourself. And if you want to start a content business for others (ghostwriting tweets, writing Substack articles for brands, etc), this is how you would bring them on as a client (I’ll give you one of the best strategies for landing your first client later).
paragraphs.zh: 这样一来，如果你想成为创作者，就可以自己执行这套流程。如果你想为别人创办内容服务业务，例如代写推文、为品牌撰写 Substack 文章等，那么你也可以按照这套方法接纳客户。稍后，我还会分享一个获取第一位客户的绝佳策略。

paragraphs.en: Step 1) Onboarding Call To Create Their Intellectual Signature
paragraphs.zh: 第一步：通过客户访谈，提炼其独特的思想标识

paragraphs.en: To make their brand and content unique, you need quite a bit of context from them.
paragraphs.zh: 要让客户的品牌和内容真正具有独特性，你需要从他们那里获得大量背景信息。

paragraphs.en: After you land them as a client, schedule a call with them so you can interview them for everything you need. Record the call so you’re able to store the transcript somewhere and reference it with AI.
paragraphs.zh: 在成功获得客户之后，安排一次通话，围绕你需要了解的所有信息对他们进行访谈。记得录下通话内容，这样你就可以将文字转录稿保存起来，并在之后借助 AI 随时查阅。

paragraphs.en: If you’re doing this for your own brand, I already have a quiz / prompt you can use. It also comes with a 30 day creator sprint course. It builds your strategy for you based off of what’s going viral right now mixed with what makes you unique.
paragraphs.zh: 如果你是为自己的品牌做这件事，我已经准备好了一份可以使用的测验和提示词。此外，它还附带一个为期 30 天的创作者冲刺课程。它会结合当下正在流行的内容，以及你自身的独特之处，为你建立品牌策略。

paragraphs.en: This is what you would ask your client, or you can ask yourself. You could also paste this into Claude and have it pull the info out of you and save it as a brand document you can reference with AI at any point.
paragraphs.zh: 以下就是你应该向客户提出的问题。当然，你也可以问自己。你还可以将这些问题粘贴到 Claude 中，让它通过与你的对话提取相关信息，并将其整理成一份品牌文档，以便随时交给 AI 参考。

paragraphs.en: All of these questions shape your brand.
paragraphs.zh: 所有这些问题共同塑造了你的品牌。

paragraphs.en: They can spin off into content topics, and are something you post about over 6-12 months. People see this and ask “How do I get this all across in one post?”
paragraphs.zh: 这些问题能够衍生出大量内容主题，足够你在未来 6 至 12 个月里持续发布。人们看到这些内容后，可能会问：「我怎样才能在一篇帖子里把所有这些东西都表达出来？」

paragraphs.en: You don’t. This is a long term game, and is why most people fail miserably. Because they want quick attention and authority. Good luck with that.
paragraphs.zh: 你不需要这样做。这是一场长期游戏，而这也正是大多数人惨败的原因：他们总想快速获得关注和权威。那就祝他们好运吧。

paragraphs.en: Since this is long, I put all of this and more into a comprehensive prompt for you, save it or duplicate it to your workspace.
paragraphs.zh: 由于这部分内容比较长，我已经把上述内容以及更多资料整理进一份完整的提示词文档中，你可以保存它，也可以将它复制到自己的工作空间。

paragraphs.en: 1. Who you help
paragraphs.zh: 1. 你帮助谁

paragraphs.en: 1. Who do you most want to help? Describe one real person.
paragraphs.zh: 1. 你最想帮助谁？请具体描述一个真实的人。

paragraphs.en: 2. What does a bad day look like for them right now?
paragraphs.zh: 2. 对他们来说，现在糟糕的一天是什么样子的？

paragraphs.en: 3. What do they say when they complain to a friend? Use their exact words.
paragraphs.zh: 3. 当他们向朋友抱怨时，会说些什么？请尽可能使用他们的原话。

paragraphs.en: 4. What have they already tried that didn’t work?
paragraphs.zh: 4. 他们已经尝试过哪些方法，但最终没有奏效？

paragraphs.en: 2. Your story
paragraphs.zh: 2. 你的故事

paragraphs.en: 1. What have you lived through that your audience is living through now?
paragraphs.zh: 1. 你曾经历过哪些事情，而你的目标受众现在也正在经历？

paragraphs.en: 2. What was the moment things changed for you (no matter how small)?
paragraphs.zh: 2. 对你而言，事情发生转变的那个时刻是什么？无论它有多么微小。

paragraphs.en: 3. What have you built, tried, failed at, or figured out? List them from biggest to smallest, they are all worthy.
paragraphs.zh: 3. 你曾经建立过什么、尝试过什么、在哪些事情上失败过，又解决或弄明白了什么？请按照从大到小的顺序全部列出来，每一件事都有价值。

paragraphs.en: 4. What results can you point to, for you or for people you’ve helped?
paragraphs.zh: 4. 你能展示哪些成果？无论是你自己取得的，还是你帮助过的人取得的。

paragraphs.en: 3. Who shaped your mind
paragraphs.zh: 3. 哪些人塑造了你的思想

paragraphs.en: 1. Whose books, posts, or videos do you never skip? Name real people and titles.
paragraphs.zh: 1. 哪些人的书籍、帖子或视频是你从来不会跳过的？请写出具体的人名和作品名称。

paragraphs.en: 2. Which idea from them do you keep coming back to, and why?
paragraphs.zh: 2. 他们提出的哪些观点让你反复思考？为什么？

paragraphs.en: 3. Who changed how you think, even if you disagree with them now?
paragraphs.zh: 3. 哪些人曾经改变了你的思维方式，即使你现在已经不再认同他们？

paragraphs.en: 4. Content pillars and unique perspective
paragraphs.zh: 4. 内容支柱与独特视角

paragraphs.en: 1. What could you talk about for hours? List everything, even things that seem unrelated.
paragraphs.zh: 1. 有哪些话题是你可以连续谈论几个小时的？请全部列出来，即使它们看起来毫不相关。

paragraphs.en: 2. Of those, which 2 or 3 matter most to you?
paragraphs.zh: 2. 在这些话题中，哪两到三个对你最重要？

paragraphs.en: 3. How do you come at each one differently from others? (For example “through psychology” or “as a former nurse”)
paragraphs.zh: 3. 对于每一个话题，你与其他人相比有什么不同的切入角度？例如「从心理学的角度」或「作为一名前护士」。

paragraphs.en: 4. What do people ask you for advice on most?
paragraphs.zh: 4. 人们最经常向你咨询哪些方面的建议？

paragraphs.en: 5. What do you keep explaining to people over and over?
paragraphs.zh: 5. 有哪些事情是你总要一遍又一遍向别人解释的？

paragraphs.en: 5. Mission and beliefs
paragraphs.zh: 5. 使命与信念

paragraphs.en: 1. In one sentence, what do you want to help people do?
paragraphs.zh: 1. 用一句话说明，你希望帮助人们实现什么。

paragraphs.en: 2. What do you believe that most people in your space don’t?
paragraphs.zh: 2. 在你所处的领域，有什么观点是你相信、但大多数同行并不认同的？

paragraphs.en: 3. What common advice in your field do you think is wrong?
paragraphs.zh: 3. 在你的领域中，你认为哪些常见建议其实是错误的？

paragraphs.en: 6. What you’re against
paragraphs.zh: 6. 你反对什么

paragraphs.en: 1. What way of living is hurting the people you want to help?
paragraphs.zh: 1. 哪种生活方式正在伤害你希望帮助的人？

paragraphs.en: 2. What life do you want to help them escape? Answer in your own words.
paragraphs.zh: 2. 你希望帮助他们摆脱怎样的生活？请用自己的语言回答。

paragraphs.en: 3. What myth or habit would you get rid of if you could? (A habit or idea, not a person or company.)
paragraphs.zh: 3. 如果可以，你最想消除哪一种迷思或习惯？注意，是一种习惯或观念，而不是某个人或某家公司。

paragraphs.en: 7. Why it matters right now
paragraphs.zh: 7. 为什么这件事在当下如此重要

paragraphs.en: 1. What just changed in the world that most people haven’t noticed yet?
paragraphs.zh: 1. 世界最近发生了什么变化，而大多数人还没有意识到？

paragraphs.en: 8. Where you’re taking them
paragraphs.zh: 8. 你将带他们走向何方

paragraphs.en: 1. What does their day-to-day life look like five years after following you?
paragraphs.zh: 1. 在关注你五年之后，他们的日常生活会变成什么样子？

paragraphs.en: 2. What would they proudly call themselves in their own bio?
paragraphs.zh: 2. 他们会在自己的个人简介中自豪地用什么身份称呼自己？

paragraphs.en: 3. Who are you in their story? (Their guide, someone documenting the journey, or someone who got out and came back with a map.)
paragraphs.zh: 3. 在他们的故事中，你扮演什么角色？是引路人、记录这段旅程的人，还是那个已经走出困境，又带着地图回来的人？

paragraphs.en: 9. Rules and words
paragraphs.zh: 9. 规则与专属表达

paragraphs.en: 1. What does your ideal reader believe and do every day? List 5 to 12 rules.
paragraphs.zh: 1. 你理想中的读者每天相信什么、践行什么？请列出 5 至 12 条规则。

paragraphs.en: 2. Do you have names for your own ideas, methods, or problems? Write each name with what it means.
paragraphs.zh: 2. 你是否为自己的观点、方法或问题起过专门的名字？请写出每个名称，并解释它的含义。

paragraphs.en: Keep all of this information somewhere safe, like a brand board in Eden so you can reference it whenever you are ideating post ideas.
paragraphs.zh: 将所有这些信息保存在一个安全的地方，例如 Eden 中的品牌资料板。这样，每当你构思帖子主题时，都可以随时查阅。

paragraphs.en: Step 2) Scrape Their Best Content If They Are Posting
paragraphs.zh: 第二步：如果客户已经在发布内容，就提取他们表现最好的作品

paragraphs.en: I think we can all agree AI can’t replicate someone’s voice.
paragraphs.zh: 我想我们都能认同一点：AI 无法真正复制一个人的表达风格。

paragraphs.en: Even if it gets close, there’s always going to be one little thing that feels off about it.
paragraphs.zh: 即使它模仿得非常接近，也总会有某个细微之处让人感觉不对劲。

paragraphs.en: That’s not our goal with this. AI can handle company voices just fine, but a personal brand is personal for a reason. It needs that hit of uniqueness.
paragraphs.zh: 但这并不是我们的目标。AI 完全可以很好地处理企业品牌的表达风格，但个人品牌之所以叫个人品牌，自然有它的原因。它需要那种鲜明的个人独特性。

paragraphs.en: The reason we interview them and pull in their best content isn’t to automate the entire process. Instead, you’re building a knowledge base of everything that is unique or noteworthy about that person. When you use AI to brainstorm, draft, or ideate, it becomes so much easier than starting from scratch.
paragraphs.zh: 我们采访客户并提取他们最优秀的内容，并不是为了自动化整个流程。相反，我们要建立一个知识库，记录这个人所有独特或值得关注的特征。这样，当你使用 AI 进行头脑风暴、起草内容或构思主题时，就不必每次都从零开始。

paragraphs.en: To pull in their best content on all platforms, connect Eden to Claude or ChatGPT with the MCP so it can pull in their posts or others posts that are going viral, give it their social handles, and use a prompt like this:
paragraphs.zh: 要提取客户在各个平台上的优秀内容，可以通过 MCP 将 Eden 连接到 Claude 或 ChatGPT，让它获取客户的帖子，以及其他正在走红的内容。然后提供客户的社交媒体账号，并使用类似下面的提示词：

paragraphs.en: Pull the best content from [@handles]. 10-20 posts from each platform they are on. Then, I want you to note down the core ideas that make them unique, the aspects of their voice that have personality, and a guess at what their worldview or philosophy is that could rally other people behind it. In essence, note down everything that led to their growth, and compile it into a document.
paragraphs.zh: 提取这些账号（[@handles]）中表现最好的内容，每个平台选择 10 至 20 篇帖子。然后，记录下让他们与众不同的核心观点、表达风格中具有个人特色的部分，以及他们可能拥有的、能够凝聚其他人的世界观或哲学理念。简而言之，记录所有促成他们成长的因素，并将这些内容整理成一份文档。

paragraphs.en: It’s also worth just looking at their top posts on all platforms so you can spot patterns that are replicable.
paragraphs.zh: 此外，也值得直接查看他们在各个平台上表现最好的帖子，从中找出可以借鉴和复用的规律。

paragraphs.en: Step 2.5) If You Haven’t Started Posting Content Yet
paragraphs.zh: 第二步半：如果你还没有开始发布内容

paragraphs.en: As a beginner, this is arguably the best thing you can do.
paragraphs.zh: 对于初学者而言，这或许是你能做的最好的事情。

paragraphs.en: You must understand that your mind has been shaped by those who have impacted you the most. Your best ideas - the ones that will lead to your growth - are how you interpret the ideas you’ve adopted from others.
paragraphs.zh: 你必须明白，你的思想是由那些对你影响最深的人塑造的。你最好的想法——那些能够推动你成长的想法——其实来自你对他人观点的理解和重新诠释。

paragraphs.en: Similar to “steal like an artist,” except it’s just how the mind works.
paragraphs.zh: 这有点类似于「像艺术家一样去偷师」，只不过这本来就是人类思维的运作方式。

paragraphs.en: It’s a core sign of intelligence to swap the beliefs and ideas running your mind when you are exposed to a new one. It is a sign of stupidity to never let go of beliefs or ideas that do not lead to advantageous outcomes.
paragraphs.zh: 当你接触到新的观点时，能够替换头脑中原有的信念和想法，这是智慧的重要表现。相反，始终不肯放弃那些无法带来积极结果的信念或观念，则是一种愚蠢。

paragraphs.en: My mind is largely composed of ideas that have been mashed together from Naval, Leo Gura, Mihaly C, Steven Kotler, Ken Wilber, and more. The interaction of those ideas in my head, plus my own life experience, is what makes my ideas mine.
paragraphs.zh: 我的思想在很大程度上是由 Naval、Leo Gura、Mihaly C、Steven Kotler、Ken Wilber 等人的观点融合而成的。这些思想在我头脑中的相互作用，再加上我自己的生活经历，最终构成了属于我自己的观点。

paragraphs.en: So, if you aren’t posting content, create a list of 5-10 people who have impacted you the most.
paragraphs.zh: 因此，如果你还没有开始发布内容，就先列出 5 至 10 位对你影响最大的人。

paragraphs.en: If they are creators, even better. Put them in a list so you can see all of their content or chat with it.
paragraphs.zh: 如果他们本身就是创作者，那就更好了。把他们整理到一个列表中，这样你就能查看他们发布的所有内容，或者直接与这些内容进行对话。

paragraphs.en: Then use the same prompt mentioned above, but for their social handles. If they don’t have social media, ask AI to pull their best ideas from across the web and their books. Save it as a document somewhere safe.
paragraphs.zh: 接着，使用前面提到的同一份提示词，只不过这次针对的是他们的社交媒体账号。如果他们没有社交媒体账号，就让 AI 从整个互联网和他们的书籍中提取最有价值的观点，并将结果保存到一个安全的地方，整理成文档。

paragraphs.en: Step 3) Create A Research-Backed Content Map
paragraphs.zh: 第三步：建立一份有研究数据支撑的内容地图

paragraphs.en: So far we have:
paragraphs.zh: 到目前为止，我们已经完成了以下工作：

paragraphs.en: Gotten enough brand context to create something unique.
paragraphs.zh: 获得了足够的品牌背景信息，以便创造出具有独特性的内容。

paragraphs.en: Documented the best ideas that we can reuse, reposition, and replicate.
paragraphs.zh: 记录了那些可以重新利用、重新定位和借鉴的优秀观点。

paragraphs.en: Now, we need to put on our marketing hat.
paragraphs.zh: 现在，我们需要戴上营销的帽子。

paragraphs.en: And it’s not even a marketing hat. It’s an artists hat.
paragraphs.zh: 不过，这甚至不是一顶营销的帽子，而是一顶艺术家的帽子。

paragraphs.en: Most “creatives” hate the thought of researching viral posts, or top performing YouTube titles, or basing your content off of what is more likely to perform... but you’re just looking at it from an angle that hides what you’re actually doing.
paragraphs.zh: 大多数所谓的「创意人士」，都不喜欢研究热门帖子、表现出色的 YouTube 标题，或者根据内容可能取得的表现来决定创作方向。但你只是从一个错误的角度看待这件事，因此没有意识到自己实际上在做什么。

paragraphs.en: You’re collecting references.
paragraphs.zh: 你其实是在收集创作参考资料。

paragraphs.en: That’s what artists do. They have inspiration boards and references that help shape their work. They don’t copy it 1-1, but they pull patterns and principles so that their own work is likely to perform better.
paragraphs.zh: 艺术家本来就是这样工作的。他们会建立灵感板，收集各种参考资料，用来塑造自己的作品。他们不会一比一照搬，而是从中提取规律和原则，让自己的作品更有可能取得好的表现。

paragraphs.en: Because let’s face it, you want your work to be a success. You just think looking at data feels icky and somehow isn’t a part of the creative process. Snap out of it.
paragraphs.zh: 说到底，你当然希望自己的作品取得成功。你只是觉得研究数据有些令人不舒服，甚至认为这不属于创作过程的一部分。别再这样想了。

paragraphs.en: Here’s what you do.
paragraphs.zh: 具体来说，你应该这样做。

paragraphs.en: Disclaimer: I’m mentioning Eden a lot in this letter, because frankly there isn’t anything else that can do the job. Social scrapers can’t see what’s performing across more than one account, and apps like GrokBot are incredible, but only work on X, and you’re better off researching platforms that you’re not posting on to get unique ideas.
paragraphs.zh: 免责声明：我在这篇文章中多次提到 Eden，因为坦白说，目前没有其他工具能够完成同样的工作。社交媒体爬虫无法跨越多个账号分析哪些内容表现出色；而 GrokBot 之类的应用虽然很强大，但只能在 X 平台上使用。为了获得独特的创意，你最好也去研究那些自己尚未发布内容的平台。

paragraphs.en: It’s as simple as using this prompt, and plugging the 2 documents you’ve made so far into it:
paragraphs.zh: 整个过程非常简单：使用下面这份提示词，并将你此前制作的两份文档输入其中即可。

paragraphs.en: I want you to create a research backed content map: 3-4 unique and broad content pillars that branch into 5-7 topics that are both based on ideas that are working, through my own unique lens based on [@brand document] and [@content document]. Branching off each topic should be 5-10 ideas that are likely to perform well, with 4-5 angles branching off of each of those ideas.
paragraphs.zh: 我希望你创建一份有研究数据支撑的内容地图：先确定 3 至 4 个独特且宽泛的内容支柱，再将每个内容支柱扩展为 5 至 7 个主题。这些主题既要建立在当前已经被验证有效的观点之上，也要通过我自己的独特视角进行重新诠释。请参考 [@品牌文档] 和 [@内容文档]。每个主题下面再延伸出 5 至 10 个有可能取得良好表现的创意，并为每个创意进一步提供 4 至 5 种切入角度。

paragraphs.en: Look over my brand and content docs, pull potential pillars and my lens out of it, then use Eden to research what’s performing across platforms in those topics. We want a unique content map, but we want to merge it with patterns that have been proven to perform over the past 6-12 months.
paragraphs.zh: 仔细查看我的品牌文档和内容文档，从中提取潜在的内容支柱以及我的独特视角，然后使用 Eden 研究这些主题在各个平台上的表现。我们希望得到一份独特的内容地图，同时也要将过去 6 至 12 个月中已经被证明有效的内容规律融入其中。

paragraphs.en: Put the output in an easy to read document.
paragraphs.zh: 请将最终结果整理成一份易于阅读的文档。

paragraphs.en: Now you have about 6 months of content ideas that you can work with. You can ask Eve or AI to draft them using the previous context we made, and validate the structure of the post based on what’s performing as well.
paragraphs.zh: 现在，你已经拥有了大约六个月的内容创意储备。你可以让 Eve 或其他 AI 根据此前建立的背景资料起草这些内容，同时参考当前表现出色的帖子，验证文章结构是否合理。

paragraphs.en: I think it’s hard to deny that you wouldn’t see results with this process, and that it puts you miles upon miles ahead of those who are not doing this.
paragraphs.zh: 我认为，很难否认这套流程能够带来成果。它会让你远远领先于那些没有采用这种方法的人。

paragraphs.en: As mentioned, here’s a doc/prompt you can duplicate with the entire process in it. It may take a bit to get through, but it is comprehensive.
paragraphs.zh: 正如前面提到的，这里还有一份可以复制的文档和提示词，其中包含了完整的操作流程。它可能需要花一些时间才能读完，但内容非常全面。

chapters.title: How to Land Your First Client
chapters.titleZh: 如何获得你的第一位客户

paragraphs.en: A few years ago, my friend JK Molina (the guy who essentially started the trend of becoming a twitter ghostwriter), send me a DM.
paragraphs.zh: 几年前，我的朋友 JK Molina 给我发了一条私信。他基本上就是在 Twitter 上开创代笔写作这一趋势的人。

paragraphs.en: It went something like this:
paragraphs.zh: 他的私信大概是这样写的：

paragraphs.en: “Dan, I know you don’t want anyone to write for you, but I wrote 10 posts for you anyway. Try posting them, if you like them, then let me write more, or just give me a testimonial.”
paragraphs.zh: 「Dan，我知道你不希望别人替你写内容，但我还是为你写好了 10 篇帖子。你可以试着发布它们。如果你喜欢，就让我继续写；或者，你只需要给我一份推荐评价就行。」

paragraphs.en: Before I was doing social media stuff, I was a freelancer, and cold outreach was pure hell. I hated it.
paragraphs.zh: 在从事社交媒体相关工作之前，我是一名自由职业者，而陌生客户开发简直就是一场噩梦。我非常讨厌这件事。

paragraphs.en: But when I got this DM, I realized this has to be one of the best strategies anyone could use to land a content client for $2500 to $5000 a month. You could target current busy creators, founders, or people just struggling to grow.
paragraphs.zh: 但当我收到这条私信时，我意识到，这一定是获取内容服务客户的最佳策略之一。你甚至可以借此获得每月支付 2,500 至 5,000 美元的客户。目标对象可以是工作繁忙的创作者、企业创始人，或者那些正为增长而苦苦挣扎的人。

paragraphs.en: You could do everything we mentioned above in one prompt for them, have it draft 10 posts, polish them up, and send 10 DMs a day.
paragraphs.zh: 你可以通过一条提示词，为他们完成前面提到的所有工作，让 AI 起草 10 篇帖子，然后由你亲自润色，最后每天发送 10 条私信。

paragraphs.en: If you actually did that, I’d find it hard to believe that you wouldn’t land atleast one client in a month.
paragraphs.zh: 如果你真的坚持这样做，我很难相信你一个月下来连一位客户都拿不到。

paragraphs.en: This is the “Permissionless Apprentice” approach.
paragraphs.zh: 这就是「无须许可的学徒式策略」（Permissionless Apprentice）。

paragraphs.en: You do free work for a dream client, then get it in front of them however you can.
paragraphs.zh: 你先为自己理想中的客户免费完成一部分工作，然后想尽一切办法让对方看到你的成果。

paragraphs.en: If DMs don’t work, do it in public like this:
paragraphs.zh: 如果私信行不通，那就像下面这样，直接公开展示你的能力。

paragraphs.en: In that reel, he hooked them in with “Grant Cardone needs a new creative director and this is my application. It seems like his content is stuck in 2016.”
paragraphs.zh: 在那条 Reels 短视频中，他用这样一句话吸引了人们的注意：「Grant Cardone 需要一位新的创意总监，而这就是我的求职申请。他的内容似乎还停留在 2016 年。」

paragraphs.en: I think Grant Cardone responding saying “Hit me I’m stuck” and the engagement on this post prove most of what I’ve said in this letter. It is a massive opportunity right now. And you have all the tools to land these clients, onboard them, and create incredible content for them.
paragraphs.zh: 我认为，Grant Cardone 回复「联系我，我现在确实陷入困境了」，以及这条帖子所获得的互动，已经证明了我在这篇文章中所说的大部分观点。当下存在着巨大的机会，而你已经拥有获取客户、完成客户入驻，以及为他们创作出色内容所需的全部工具。

paragraphs.en: Hope this was helpful.
paragraphs.zh: 希望这些内容对你有所帮助。

paragraphs.en: – Dan
paragraphs.zh: ——Dan

paragraphs.en: Again, workshop on how to write newsletters / articles people can’t help but read happens on November 10. Join here if you want to learn to create long-form content as a skill.
paragraphs.zh: 最后再提醒一次：关于如何撰写让人忍不住阅读的新闻通讯和文章的工作坊，将于 11 月 10 日举行。如果你希望将长篇内容创作培养成一项专业技能，可以在这里报名参加。
